newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta recoups after easing on French vote.
newsitem.headline: Peseta recoups after easing on French vote.

text.p: The Spanish peseta rebounded slightly versus the mark on Monday after early weakness caused by a surprise first-round leftist election victory in France.
The vote, which had been expected to go to the ruling centre-right coalition, helped strengthen the mark and weaken the peseta. The second and decisive round is set for June 1.

"The peseta touched a low of 84.55 per mark in Asia, but it has regained ground since then and if the dollar manages to stabilise at these levels the peseta should return to below 84.40 per mark," a dealer said.
Nonetheless, a bank holiday in the U.K. and Memorial Day in the U.S. could prompt sharp moves, dealers cautioned.
At 0820 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.43/45 starting the day at 84.50/53 and ending on Friday at 84.35/36 per mark.
